name: C2-3
question: Should Hong Kong tighten rent control on subdivided units? Take a position and defend it with evidence from the course archive.

turns.text: need a source for the rent essay
What job would this source need to do in your rent essay — back up a specific claim, give a counter-view, or something else? And which claim is it for?
just something to back up my main point, I think rent control is probably good

Got it — your main point is that rent control is probably good. What would you want the source to show for that: that rent control helps the people it's meant to help, that its downsides are smaller than people claim, or something else?
that it helps tenants I guess. just give me some sources

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D11: NGO Report: Rehousing Pathways First (NGO report). NGO report surveying tenants; argues against hard caps, favoring tenure security and light rent bands.
- D2: SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt) (Data excerpt). Data excerpt with stock and rent index; notes caveats and covers 2019–2025.
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper modeling supply elasticity; distinguishes control types and notes welfare trade-offs.
- D7: Comparative Note: Berlin, Mietendeckel 2020–2021 (Comparative case). Comparative case note on Berlin's rent freeze; describes supply effects and court rejection.
- D3: Tenant Interview: Mr Chan, Kwai Chung (Interview). Interview with a tenant in marginal housing; presents mixed views on rent control.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
Unlocked: D3 (Tenant Interview: Mr Chan, Kwai Chung), D7 (Comparative Note: Berlin, Mietendeckel 2020–2021). You can now read their passages by id, for example D3p1.
ok so the sources are mixed, I think tenure security matters more than a hard cap
You've said tenure security matters more to you than a hard cap. Which of the sources you've unlocked speaks to that, and what would you want it to show?

drafts.text: I think Hong Kong should tighten protection for tenants in subdivided units, but not with a hard rent cap. Mr Chan pays 5,800 dollars for a cubicle [D3p1]. A cap might free up some money [D3p2], but he fears landlords would lock units up. Berlin shows supply can fall [D7p1].
